info.name: ScoreGrid API
info.description:
Live walkthrough of the ScoreGrid API through the gateway: platform checks, the admin and participant journeys, asynchronous scoring, every contract error code, the failover companion requests and an endpoint reference.

Use with the **ScoreGrid local** environment. Set `adminPassword` there (the `SCOREGRID_ADMIN_PASSWORD` value from `.env`; it is never stored in the repository). Headless: `scripts/api-tests.sh`.

Run 00-04 and 06 in order (the Collection Runner keeps the ids each request captures). 05 is manual. Every run creates fresh users, teams and tournaments; nothing is deleted.

Contract: docs/contracts.md. Runbook: docs/demo.md. Details: postman/README.md.

item.name: 05 Failover (manual)
item.description:
**Manual. Excluded from `scripts/api-tests.sh`.** Companion to `scripts/failover-demo.sh` (docs/demo.md#failover). Run 01-04 first: these requests reuse their tokens and tournament.

Before any scenario: `scripts/failover-demo.sh status` must show two TOURNAMENT-SERVICE instances (else `scripts/failover-demo.sh restore`). After the demo: `scripts/failover-demo.sh restore`, then `scripts/smoke.sh`.

Each request says which terminal command to run first.

item.name: Instance failover: list tournaments (repeat in the Runner)

request.description:
**Terminal first:** `scripts/failover-demo.sh instance`

Start the Runner with only this request at the same time: 420 iterations, 500 ms delay (about 4 min, the whole scenario; 40 iterations cover just the SIGTERM window). Every iteration must be 200: the gateway retries a GET that hits the dead replica on the live one. Expect about ten slow iterations (1-6 s) right after the stop and the kill.

item.name: Downstream failover, step 1: create a fresh open match

request.description: **Send BEFORE starting the scenario**, while both tournament replicas are up: it is a write, and writes are never retried by the gateway. Each send creates a new match, so step 2 can be repeated.

item.name: Downstream failover, step 2: predict while a tournament replica is dead

exec: pm.test('prediction accepted with one replica dead', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().matchId).to.eql(pm.variables.get('failoverMatchId')));

request.description:
**Terminal first:** `scripts/failover-demo.sh downstream`. Send this as soon as it prints `SIGKILL ...` (the replica stays dead until the script restarts it).

Expect 201. Prediction Service checks the enrolment against tournament-service; an attempt that lands on the dead replica fails its 0.5 s connect timeout and the retry goes to the live one (about 0.7 s, under 3 s). Step 1 again before resending: a second prediction on the same match is `DUPLICATE_PREDICTION`.

exec: pm.test('contract error envelope with error = DOWNSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE', () => {
pm.test('answered within the gateway time limit (< 8 s)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.below(8000));

request.description:
**Terminal first:** `scripts/failover-demo.sh service-down`. Send while it prints its twelve probes; prediction-service stays down until it prints `starting prediction-service again`, and the gateway keeps answering 503 for ~15 s more while the replica boots.

For a slower pace on stage: `docker compose stop prediction-service`, send as often as you like, then `scripts/failover-demo.sh restore`.

Expect `503 DOWNSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` in the contract envelope. The first call right after the stop can take 3-6 s: the gateway may still hold the stopped replica's address and spends its 2 s connect timeout on each attempt. Once four calls have failed the breaker opens, and every later call answers in milliseconds without trying. Send it two or three times.
